title: Geometric signed compatibility of completed integral twist lines
statement: The scheme-naturality clause of integral twist base change: for a scheme morphism h and finite coefficient embedding E to F, the canonical coefficient and root comparisons extend to signed additive inverse-image isomorphisms. They preserve the coefficient unit, roots tensor, scalar action, positive tensor recursion and negative evaluation, and commute with the scalar-inclusion maps in every integer degree. Uses [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], [lem-pur-integral-twist-line-inverse-image], [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], [def-pur-sheaf-hom], [def-weil-integral-twist-inverse-comparison].

source.place: Final scheme-naturality sentence; original integral base-change proof step 8.

proof.text: Linearize the coefficient and degree-one inverse-image comparisons through the module adjunction. For an isomorphic structural coefficient map, scalar extension is restriction along the inverse; hence the underlying module pullback is the actual additive inverse image, with its unit sections.

Apply the normalized signed-line scalar pullback square to the four rank-one integral first lines. The scalar identifications are determined by their pure-tensor formulas; uniqueness identifies them with the canonical twistScalarMaps family. Transport the resulting signed pullbacks to additive inverse images. The generic unit, tensor and evaluation normalizations give the required normalization predicate. Its all-degree square gives the required equality by injectivity of the additive adjunction hom equivalence.

proof_origin.place: J4: canonical scalar specifications and tower theorem directly; geometric signed-family clause isolated.

theorem integral_twist_base_change_scheme
    (F : Type u) [Field F] [Algebra (Padic l) F] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) F]
    (ι : E →ₐ[Padic l] F) (S : Scheme.{u})
    [∀ x : S, Invertible (l : S.residueField x)] :
    ∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (h : X ⟶ S)
        [∀ x : X, Invertible (l : X.residueField x)],
      ∃ (αE : (proEtaleSheafInverseImage h CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj
          (completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E S) ⟶
            completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l E X)
        (αF : (proEtaleSheafInverseImage h CommRingCat.{u + 1}).obj
          (completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l F S) ⟶
            completedIntegralCommRingSheafUnrestricted l F X)
        (τ : (proEtaleSheafInverseImage h AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
          (purTwistZlOne S l) ⟶ purTwistZlOne X l)
        (ρE : ∀ m : ℤ, (proEtaleSheafInverseImage h AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
          (integralTwistUnderlying l E S m) ≅ integralTwistUnderlying l E X m)
        (ρF : ∀ m : ℤ, (proEtaleSheafInverseImage h AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
          (integralTwistUnderlying l F S m) ≅ integralTwistUnderlying l F X m),
        (IsIso αE ∧ IsPurIntegralCoefficientComparison h l E αE) ∧
        (IsIso αF ∧ IsPurIntegralCoefficientComparison h l F αF) ∧
        (IsIso τ ∧ IsPurRootLimitComparison h l τ) ∧
        IsIntegralTwistInverseComparison l E h αE τ ρE ∧
        IsIntegralTwistInverseComparison l F h αF τ ρF ∧
        (proEtaleSheafInverseImage h CommRingCat.{u + 1}).map
            (integralCompletedScalarMap l E F ι S) ≫ αF =
          αE ≫ integralCompletedScalarMap l E F ι X ∧
        ∀ m : ℤ,
          (proEtaleSheafInverseImage h AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).map
              (integralTwistScalarUnderlying l E S F ι m) ≫ (ρF m).hom =
            (ρE m).hom ≫ integralTwistScalarUnderlying l E X F ι m
